findings.statement: CA9 is up in all three layers: RNA log2FC 6.312 (padj 1.72e-49), protein log2FC 2.269 (padj 9.9e-43), phospho log2FC 1.91 (padj 5.18e-30). RNA-protein Spearman rho 0.797 (padj 6.48e-24); 9p loss frequency 0.145. A HIF-driven membrane enzyme, it is a strong tissue-biomarker and surface-target candidate.

CD70 is up in RNA (log2FC 4.464, padj 4.13e-35) and protein (log2FC 2.421, padj 1.94e-38), with RNA-protein rho 0.843 (padj 4e-29), the highest concordance among the candidates; CNV is minimal (gain 0.027, loss 0.009). A surface ligand with very large tumor-normal difference, consistent with an antibody/cell-therapy target.

EGFR is top of the convergence ranking (score 3.87, 5 streams). Up in RNA (log2FC 1.461, padj 1.76e-23), protein (log2FC 1.062, padj 7.32e-45) and phospho (log2FC 0.874, padj 1.99e-37); rho 0.699; 7p gain frequency 0.255. Effect sizes are modest but layer-concordant, with approved EGFR drugs available.

MET is up in RNA (log2FC 1.342, padj 1.19e-21), protein (log2FC 1.101, padj 1.42e-34) and phospho (log2FC 0.723, padj 8.03e-19); rho 0.817 (padj 5.62e-26); 7q gain frequency 0.255. Kinase activity signal supports MET as a druggable target (rank 6 in convergence).

COXFA4L2 (dataset symbol NDUFA4L2) has the largest tumor-normal change: RNA log2FC 6.752 (padj 1.66e-49), protein log2FC 3.768 (padj 5.99e-48), phospho log2FC 2.598; rho 0.634; 12q gain frequency 0.118. It is a hypoxia-driven mitochondrial gene, a top tissue biomarker rather than an obvious surface target.

NNMT is up in RNA (log2FC 4.67, padj 2.04e-40) and protein (log2FC 2.709, padj 1.23e-43); rho 0.634 (padj 6.46e-13); no marked CNV (loss 0.045, gain 0.027). Concordant across layers; metabolic enzyme with a small-molecule-inhibitor rationale and biomarker value.

PLIN2 is up in protein (log2FC 2.667, padj 7.99e-44), phospho (log2FC 1.9) and RNA (log2FC 2.62, padj 2.37e-26), reflecting lipid-droplet accumulation of ccRCC; RNA-protein rho is only 0.336 (padj 0.000618) and 9p loss frequency 0.164, so protein-level measurement is preferable.

ENO2 is up in RNA (log2FC 3.538, padj 4.81e-39), protein (log2FC 2.245, padj 2.91e-44) and phospho (log2FC 1.84); rho 0.716 (padj 1.78e-17); 12p gain frequency 0.118. Glycolytic marker consistent with the Warburg-like ccRCC phenotype.

SLC16A3 (MCT4, lactate exporter) is up in RNA (log2FC 3.435, padj 3.3e-49), protein (log2FC 2.279, padj 5.43e-47) and phospho (log2FC 1.48); membrane transporter with minimal CNV (gain 0.036, loss 0.018), a plausible metabolic target.

ALDOB is strongly down in RNA (log2FC -7.028, padj 9.42e-31), protein (log2FC -2.273, padj 2.07e-40) and phospho (log2FC -1.415), reflecting loss of proximal-tubule identity; a negative tissue biomarker, not a target. 9p loss frequency 0.164.

VHL sits on 3p with loss frequency 0.791 (gain 0.027) and is reduced in RNA (log2FC -0.479, padj 1.62e-17) and protein (log2FC -0.172, padj 0.04), the founding event behind HIF activation and the CA9/NDUFA4L2 signature. The protein change is small and borderline.

PBRM1 (3p) has copy-number loss frequency 0.8 (gain 0.027) with modest reductions in RNA (log2FC -0.238, padj 1.16e-08), protein (log2FC -0.265, padj 6.76e-12) and phospho (log2FC -0.246). Tumor-suppressor loss is a driver mechanism, not a directly targetable product.

caveats: CPTAC discovery cohort only (110 tumors; 75 RNA and 84 proteome/phosphoproteome matched normals); no independent validation was performed here.
Bulk tumor-vs-normal differences can reflect immune/stromal infiltration or tissue composition, not only tumor-cell expression.
Omics supports expression and copy number only; surface localization, druggability and safety were not assessed from these data beyond the convergence ranking.
Several cnv_frequency results (CA9, EGFR, MET, CD70, NNMT, PLIN2, ENO2, ALDOB, SLC16A3, COXFA4L2) have no evidence id, so CNV values are quoted without citation.
COXFA4L2 is the dataset symbol NDUFA4L2; EGFR/MET gains are arm-level 7p/7q events, not focal amplifications.
